{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Frank D. Grosshans''' (born 1942)<ref>{{cite web |title=Frank Grosshans |url=https://aleph.nkp.cz/F/?func=find-c&local_base=aut&ccl_term=ica=uk20211110594 |website=Czech National Authority Database |access-date=23 February 2025}}</ref> is an American mathematician who works in [[invariant theory]], where he is known for the discovery of [[Grosshans subgroup]]s and [[Grosshans graded coefficient]]s.<ref>The Mathematical Association of America website, Talk Abstract, "The Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Functions: then and now," http://math.moravian.edu/~epadel/archives/2009_03_Gettysburg/abstracts/index.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120308075608/http://math.moravian.edu/~epadel/archives/2009_03_Gettysburg/abstracts/index.html |date=2012-03-08 }} (last accessed June 17, 2010)</ref>  He is a professor of mathematics at [[West Chester University of Pennsylvania|West Chester University]], Pennsylvania.<ref name="WestChester">West Chester University, Department of Mathematics website, http://www.wcupa.edu/Academics/SCH_CAS.MAT/faculty/fgrosshans.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927143608/http://www.wcupa.edu/Academics/SCH_CAS.MAT/faculty/fgrosshans.html |date=2011-09-27 }} (last accessed June 17, 2010)</ref> Grosshans has been an invited speaker at meetings of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://math.moravian.edu/~epadel/schedule/ |title=MAA EPaDel Spring Meeting at Gettysburg College conferences |access-date=2009-03-31 |archive-date=2009-04-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090427003659/http://math.moravian.edu/~epadel/schedule/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He received his B.S. from the [[University of Illinois]] and his Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="WestChester" /> He taught at [[University of Pennsylvania]] and [[Johns Hopkins University]] before joining the West Chester University.
